record.original_question: Are Burger–Mozes’ examples of simple groups orderable?

evidence.quote: Question 3.6 (Well-Known). Are Burger–Mozes’ examples of simple groups orderable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A group $G$ is called left-orderable if there exists a total order $\le$ on $G$ that is invariant under left multiplication, i.e., $g \le h$ implies $fg \le fh$ for all $f,g,h \in G$.

Burger and Mozes constructed the first examples of finitely presented torsion-free simple groups as follows. Let $T_m$ and $T_n$ denote the $m$-regular and $n$-regular trees (with $m,n$ sufficiently large even integers). Their automorphism groups $\mathrm{Aut}(T_m)$ and $\mathrm{Aut}(T_n)$ are locally compact, and one can choose closed vertex-transitive subgroups $H_m \le \mathrm{Aut}(T_m)$ and $H_n \le \mathrm{Aut}(T_n)$ whose local actions at vertices realize prescribed finite permutation groups (for instance, alternating groups of large degree). For appropriate choices, there exist cocompact lattices $\Gamma \le H_m \times H_n$ whose projection to each factor is dense, and finite-index subgroups $\Gamma_0 \le \Gamma$ of such lattices yield finitely presented torsion-free simple groups.

Question: Is every such Burger–Mozes simple group left-orderable? Equivalently, does every group $\Gamma_0$ in this family admit a left-invariant total order?
artifact.category_tag: Orderable groups / lattices in products of trees
artifact.status_search_result: The left-orderability of the Burger–Mozes simple groups (lattices in products of trees) remains an open question. Recent work on finitely presented left-orderable simple groups (e.g., Hyde–Lodha–Rivas and related constructions) produces different examples; the Burger–Mozes case is still unresolved, with the additional remark that, by simplicity, if any of them were left-orderable they would be "left-orderable monsters."

status_evidence.title: Finitely presented left orderable monsters
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of lattices in products of trees and Burger–Mozes groups whose left-orderability is still an open question.
status_evidence.claim: Left-orderability of Burger–Mozes groups is open.

status_evidence.title: Finitely presented simple left-orderable groups in the landscape of Thompson's groups
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs finitely presented simple left-orderable groups distinct from Burger–Mozes; the Burger–Mozes case is not addressed by these constructions.
status_evidence.claim: New left-orderable simple group examples exist, but Burger–Mozes left-orderability is not resolved by them.

status_evidence.title: Finitely presented simple groups and products of trees (Burger–Mozes)
status_evidence.snippet: Original construction of finitely presented torsion-free simple groups as lattices in products of trees.
